proposal.explanation: Discovery traces confirm the SPI clock (o_sck/o_sclk) toggles at system-clock rate instead of the configured divider rate. The first mismatch at cycle 101 shows o_sck=1 when 0 is expected, and subsequent cycles show it stuck high. The root cause is the bit-transmission loop (lines 250-268) toggling SCK and advancing state every cycle without checking r_z_counter. The fix gates both the SCK-falling and SCK-rising edges with r_z_counter so the divider controls SPI frequency. Additionally, the HOTIDLE state (lines 241-248) forced the last transmitted bit to 1 and advanced state by one extra step, corrupting back-to-back byte transmission; the fix makes HOTIDLE identical to IDLE for correct serial bit order. Both edits preserve the public interface, startup timing, and Wishbone-qualified acknowledgments.

proposal.explanation: Two functional defects were repaired in the llsdspi module. First, the HOTIDLE state incorrectly forced the last transmitted bit to 1 and advanced the state machine by one extra step, corrupting the serial bit order for back-to-back bytes. The fix makes the HOTIDLE path identical to the IDLE path: load the full byte, set state to START, and hold SCK high. Second, the SPI clock divider (r_z_counter) was not used to pace the bit transmission loop; the state machine toggled SCK every system clock cycle regardless of the configured divider. The fix gates the SCK toggling and state advancement in the bit-transmission branches with r_z_counter, so the SPI clock frequency respects the i_speed divider. Both changes preserve the public port interface, startup timing, and Wishbone-qualified acknowledgments.
